clue.text: Reward staggering, but no end to poverty

indicators.note: staggering means reeling unsteadily, so the letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the end to a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A prize so huge it astonishes, yet it fails to lift anyone out of poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggering' looks like praise for the reward but is the anagram signal, turning BUT NO into BOUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A generous payment offered for a deed, such as catching an outlaw, is a reward.

clue.text: Clanger: left out large fixed capital

indicators.note: something left out is omitted from the word it was in

parts.note: a bell is something that clangs
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
fast means firmly fixed, as in stuck fast

explanation.surface: A clumsy blunder results in a big item being left out and a deadline fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clanger' suggests a gaffe but is literally a thing that clangs.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Nothing outstanding, no ring, no spouse!

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: having no spouse, i.e. single

indicators.note: no here means without, so the ring letter is removed

parts.note: unowed means with no debt outstanding
O is a ring, from its round shape

explanation.surface: Someone sums up their situation: no debts, no wedding ring, no partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has never married has no husband or wife, so is single.

clue.text: Inca dances, led by bird, that didn't go down well

definitions.note: the ship is described by a phrase standing in for the noun

indicators.note: the dancing letters are led by the bird, which comes first

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: dances suggests movement, so the letters of Inca jig about

explanation.surface: A troupe of Incas dances behind a bird, and the show is a flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'didn't go down well' sounds like a poor reception; the famous liner went down very badly indeed, sinking in 1912.
explanation.definitionFit: The White Star liner sank on its maiden voyage, so ironically it did go down, and not well.

clue.text: Very brief dance around yard

indicators.note: the dance word goes around the yard abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: a fling is a lively Scottish dance, as in the Highland fling

explanation.surface: A quick little jig performed in a back yard.
explanation.definitionFit: A visit described this way is hasty and short, as in a whistle-stop call.

clue.text: Building's unprofitable, as well as lacking love

parts.note: lean years are unprofitable ones

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the love letter is dropped

parts.note: too means as well
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A building turns out to be a poor investment and loveless besides.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple shed or structure propped against a wall is a small building.

clue.text: California-located, hilarious people working together

parts.note: located in a place: the word in
CA is the postal abbreviation for California
a very funny person is called a hoot

explanation.surface: A troupe of funny Californians collaborates.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the hyphenated 'California-located' as 'located in California': the location word comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means colluding or in league, often secretly, so cooperating.

clue.text: Dress put on mature bull

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece put on another sits above it

parts.note: garb is clothing or dress
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: Someone dresses up a fully grown bull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bull' looks like the animal but is slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bull, short for a coarser word, means nonsense or rubbish talk.

clue.text: Showing an ironic sort of loving care, secret minder fiddled with electronic implant

definitions.text: an ironic sort of loving care

indicators.note: an implant is set inside, so the electronic letter is inserted
fiddled with means tampered with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A covert guardian, sinister in their care, tampers with an electronic implant in someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddled with' rearranges SECRET MINDER and 'implant' puts E in. 'Showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical phrase is used sarcastically for harsh treatment passed off as kindness.

clue.text: See 27
Old-time dance from theatre's top male surgeons?

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
surgeons lance boils, so whimsically they are people who lance

explanation.surface: A ballroom number performed by a troupe of medics in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that surgeons are only playfully called lancers; in an operating theatre the pun is doubled.
explanation.definitionFit: This quadrille was a popular Victorian set dance for several couples, long out of fashion.

clue.text: I didn't catch that release

definitions.meaning: a polite request to repeat something not heard
to free someone from punishment, as a king or governor may

explanation.definitionFit: The word serves both as a request to hear again and as an official act of forgiveness freeing an offender.

clue.text: European match abandoned — accepted by Brown

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken in, so it goes inside

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild and unrestrained, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A football fixture is called off and a man named Brown takes it in his stride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a surname but is the colour; 'abandoned' gives TCHMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Netherlands is a European.

clue.text: Central company in theatre production

indicators.note: the company abbreviation sits in the middle of the rearranged letters
a production is something made or staged, so the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A key theatrical troupe stars in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' gives ATTHERE, which wraps the company abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being at the heart or essence of something, so fundamental or central.

clue.text: Compact newspaper? That's novel

parts.note: compact earth is packed hard
The Times is a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A query about a tabloid-sized newspaper, answered with an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: A compact is also a small-format newspaper, and 'novel' reads as 'new' before turning out to be the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens wrote this book set in industrial Coketown, published in 1854.

clue.text: Shrub came back to life — army mobilised!

parts.note: rose, as in rose from the dead

indicators.note: mobilised means set in motion, so the letters of army move about

explanation.surface: A plant revives just as troops are called up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came back to life' is the past tense 'rose' (from the dead), not the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic evergreen herb grows as a small bush, so it is a shrub.

clue.text: See 15
Got the wrong idea Adam is too kind at heart

indicators.note: at the heart of the phrase lie the letters needed, spanning the words

explanation.surface: Someone misjudged Adam, who is really too kind.
explanation.definitionFit: To err in understanding, taking one thing for another, is to misunderstand.

clue.text: Stuffing knocked out of Lulu in break of service — retiring

indicators.note: the pick from the singer's name goes in the middle of the broken letters
a break of a word smashes its letters into a new order
with the stuffing knocked out a word is left with only its outer letters

explanation.surface: The singer Lulu is soundly beaten at tennis after her serve is broken, and decides to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: Lulu is a Scottish pop singer; 'break of' gives RECSIVE, and the tennis surface hides the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A shy, retiring person avoids company and keeps to themselves.

clue.text: City relieving poor Uncle Remus of total raised

indicators.note: relieving the name of something takes it away
poor suggests the letters are in bad shape and need reordering
in a down entry raising a word reads it upwards, backwards

parts.note: a sum is a total

explanation.surface: Relief arrives for the impoverished storyteller Uncle Remus after someone collects money for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relieving' takes MUS (SUM, 'raised') from UNCLE REMUS and 'poor' shuffles what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: This Swiss city stands on its lake beneath Mount Pilatus.

clue.text: Year after Hugo's first success

indicators.note: the year letter comes after the novelist's forename

parts.note: the French novelist Hugo's first name was Victor

explanation.surface: A year on from a writer's breakthrough triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hugo's first' looks like the letter H but means the forename of Victor Hugo.
explanation.definitionFit: A win or triumph in a contest is a success.

clue.text: Sweep following round Peeler?

indicators.note: the sweep word follows the round letter

parts.note: O is round in shape
a range is a sweep or extent, as of hills or vision

explanation.surface: A chimney sweep trails a policeman on his round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peeler' is old British slang for a police officer, after Robert Peel; the question mark makes it simply a fruit you peel.
explanation.definitionFit: This citrus fruit has a thick rind that must be removed before eating, so it is a thing peeled.

clue.text: Secret drinker comes to earth in Morecambe?

indicators.note: the drinker comes to the earth letter, so it follows it

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earth, as on electrical plugs
a sot is a habitual drunkard
Eric Morecambe was half of the comedy duo Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: A closet drinker sobers up and lands back down to earth in the seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe looks like the Lancashire resort, but the question mark flags the British comedian Eric Morecambe, so it gives his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge understood only by an initiated few is obscure and private, hence secret.

clue.text: High Court division disposes of hollow ruby, making fortune

indicators.note: disposing of letters gets rid of them from the longer word

parts.note: Chancery is a division of the English High Court

indicators.note: a hollow word has lost its insides, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A judge throws out a worthless gem in court and makes a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' leaves RY from ruby; 'disposes of' takes RY off CHANCERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Luck or fate deciding what happens is synonymous with fortune.

clue.text: Louse's elevated state kept under wraps

indicators.note: in a down entry an elevated word is turned upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for the US state Pennsylvania
hid means concealed

explanation.surface: A lousy fellow keeps his intoxicated condition secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated state' tempts as 'high', but 'elevated' turns PA upwards to AP.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenfly or plant louse is a small sap-sucking insect.

clue.text: Take butterfly and name 'Bambi'?

parts.note: the comma is a species of butterfly with a white comma-shaped mark
Bambi is the young deer of the Disney film

explanation.surface: Naming a butterfly after the Disney fawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is only a link here, not part of the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize something for official or military use is to take it over by force.

clue.text: Folk hero's bonnet

definitions.meaning: the Sherwood Forest outlaw Robin, who robbed the rich
a soft head covering, or in US English the cover over a car's engine

explanation.definitionFit: Robin of Sherwood bears this surname, and the word also names a bonnet-like head covering or an engine cover.

clue.text: Musical token of affection cut short by opera house

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter

parts.note: a kiss is a token of affection
the Met is New York's Metropolitan Opera House

explanation.surface: A show-tune performer's love token is curtailed by the management of an opera house.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1953 Broadway show set in old Baghdad is a stage musical.

clue.text: Strong punch that would make you croak?

definitions.meaning: a strike that would kill you, croak being slang for die

explanation.definitionFit: A killing stroke is both a hard punch and, literally, one that makes you die, croak being slang for die.
